protocol.label_zh: 基于 PKE/KEM 的双向认证密钥交换

overview_classification.summary_label_zh: NTRU/RLWE 格基、PKE/KEM 型双向认证两消息 AKE

authentication.mechanism: Both parties hold long-term NEV-PKE-OW keys; each encrypts a fresh contribution to the peer's static key, verifies deterministic re-encryption after decryption, and binds both identities and messages into H.

roles.key_details: Static NEV-PKE-OW key plus rejection secret s_i; generates a fresh NEV-KEM-OW pair (fpk,fsk) and sends (c_j,fpk).
Static NEV-PKE-OW key plus rejection secret s_j; encrypts m_i to pki and encapsulates eK to fpk.

pre_distributed_material: Authenticated long-term NEV-AKE public keys pk_i and pk_j

forward_secrecy.conditions: Claimed through CK+ security/freshness; the model explicitly covers KCI and wPFS attacks, subject to its freshness restrictions and random-oracle assumptions.

protocol_characteristics.key_confirmation: Implicit mutual confirmation through successful PKE verification, ephemeral KEM agreement and the common hash-derived session key; no third confirmation message.
protocol_characteristics.transcript_binding: H (or H_init/H_resp on rejection) includes i,j,M,M' and the recovered/generated contributions.
protocol_characteristics.identity_binding: Ordered party identities i,j are inputs to the final hash together with both protocol messages.

technical_classification.construction_paradigm: GC-AKE two-pass transform from OW-CPA PKE and OW-CPA KEM, instantiated by NEV-PKE-OW and NEV-KEM-OW.

underlying_primitives.name: NEV-PKE-OW
underlying_primitives.role: OW-CPA static public-key encryption contribution in each direction

underlying_primitives.name: G
underlying_primitives.role: Derives deterministic PKE encryption randomness from the plaintext

hard_problems.name: Decisional NTRU
hard_problems.role: Hardness of the NEV public-key structure

hard_problems.name: sspRLWR
hard_problems.role: Additional rounding-based assumption for compressed C1*/C2*/C3* variants only

components.name: c_j
components.semantics: NEV-PKE-OW encryption of fresh m_j under responder pk_j with randomness G(m_j).

components.name: fpk
components.semantics: Fresh NEV-KEM-OW public key generated by the initiator.

components.name: c_i
components.semantics: NEV-PKE-OW encryption of fresh m_i under initiator pk_i with randomness G(m_i).

components.name: e_c
components.semantics: NEV-KEM-OW ciphertext under fpk, yielding ephemeral key eK.

protocol_flow.semantics: M'=(c_i,e_c); each party verifies/decrypts its incoming static PKE contribution and derives the key with H or an implicit-rejection hash.

static_contributions: m_j encrypted to responder static pk_j and recovered with sk_j
m_i encrypted to initiator static pk_i and recovered with sk_i
key_schedule.transcript_hash: The final random-oracle input contains m_i,m_j,eK,i,j,M,M'.
key_schedule.session_key_derivation: On valid ciphertexts: K_i,j=H(m_i,m'_j,eK,i,j,M,M') and K'_i,j=H(m'_i,m_j,fK',i,j,M,M'); deterministic re-encryption makes the valid values coincide. H_resp or H_init with the party rejection secret is used on PKE verification failure.
key_schedule.domain_separation: Implementation domains: G=0x01, H=0x02, H_init=0x03, H_resp=0x04.
key_schedule.ephemeral_secret_erasure: The specification does not give a dedicated erasure algorithm; fsk and other per-session state should be erased after Derinit, but this is not separately mandated in the protocol pseudocode.

correctness.session_failure_probability: At most the sum of two NEV-PKE-OW decryption failures and one NEV-KEM-OW decapsulation failure; <=3*delta when the component bounds coincide.
correctness.relationship: GC-AKE correctness follows from its PKE and KEM components; one completed session performs two PKE decryptions and one KEM decapsulation.
correctness.basis: Specification pp. 17, 24-25 (Algorithms 3-4 and Table 2); the factor-three session bound is a union-bound derivation.

security_claims.claim: Mutual authentication from two static PKE contributions, deterministic re-encryption checks and identity/message-bound hashing.
GC-AKE and NEV-AKE are claimed CK+ secure under ROM and QROM analyses from OW-CPA PKE/KEM assumptions.
The CK+ model used is stated to cover KCI and weak-perfect-forward-secrecy attacks.
Worst-case-message DFR analysis avoids assuming independent coefficient failures for uncompressed recommended variants.

claimed_advantages.claim: Provides ROM and QROM CK+ proofs while requiring only OW-CPA PKE and KEM.
Two-message construction with one fewer hash evaluation than HKSU in the compared responder derivation.
Small moduli and partial NTT arithmetic support portable and AVX2 implementations.
Recommended variants use a conservative failure analysis without the disproven independent-coefficient-failure heuristic.

limitations_and_constraints.description: H, H_init, H_resp and G are modeled as random oracles; the proof is ROM/QROM rather than standard-model.
All variants have nonzero component decryption failure and three correctness-relevant decryption/decapsulation events per session.
C1*/C2*/C3* ciphertext compression introduces a rounding-based sspRLWR assumption, an independence heuristic for rounding error, and implicit rejection requirements.
Both long-term public keys must be authenticated before the exchange.
Reported reference/AVX2 measurements use an AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D platform.

review_notes: All message totals were recomputed from params.h formulas; R1/R2/R3 totals match specification performance Table 4.
Nine PARAMS variants are recorded: three compressed C*, three uncompressed C, and three recommended R.
Long-term secret size follows AKE_SK_BYTES=2*POLY_BYTES+SEED_BYTES; initiator state follows AKE_ST_BYTES.
Independent review against the specification confirmed the two-message/one-round-trip flow, mutual static-key authentication construction, and every tabulated communication total.
conflicts: Specification prose names compressed variants C1*/C2*/C3*, while implementation directories/comments use -C and PARAMS=1..3; aliases preserve both forms.

issues.description: The basic-information PDF yielded no extractable text and appears scanned; submitters/affiliations were taken from specification p. 1 and unavailable Chinese names were left null.
The specification gives component DFRs but not an explicit session-level formula; <=3*delta is derived by union bound from the two PKE decryptions and one KEM decapsulation.
No explicit erasure step was found in the protocol pseudocode.
